items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: All the Black violin players have lost their jobs because Jolson has made the movie, The Sound Of Jazz [sic] or something, and no more pit bands in the Regal.

ctx.x: And we went in the Club Rubaiyat, and worked in the Club Rubaiyat on the North Side, which was a gangster-run place. That's where I got to meet Dick Stabile who is here in New Orleans, a bandleader. His father was a violin player, and Dick Stabile was a saxophone player, sensational, with Ben Bernie's band -- and he used to bring his father over to hear Eddie South.

Now, what I was going to...what I wanted to bring this to here was about Charles Elgar. Now, after this, Charles Elgar didn't get much work. He began to get around to where he didn't get much work. I didn't see him playing any place any more. Now the violins... This is, of course, 1927. The violins are all out of the business.
